page.heading: Familiar favorites. Clearer accents.
page.intro: Compare each source recording with two variations featuring a prominent cultural instrument. Audio references guide the new performances; exact melody preservation is not guaranteed. Scores assess the written briefs: the automated listening analysis proved inconsistent. Lightning remains in development.

cards.title: Hono / Banked Fire
cards.description: The calm Fire take, with an exposed koto phrase and an unmistakable bend after its held note.
cards.listen_for: A prominent natural Japanese koto carries the existing lead contour. Hear its firm plucked attack, resonant string decay, and a clear left-hand pitch bend AFTER the held note begins. Expose one short solo koto phrase, then bring the same koto hook back into the original warm groove. The acoustic gesture must be clearly audible rather than buried as a decorative texture.

cards.title: Tanka / Weight Without Hurry
cards.description: Keep Metal’s held weight; a clear wooden-flute voice traces the broad descending melody over a sparse deep drum.
cards.listen_for: Add a foreground solo traditional wooden Plains flute as an instrumental connection to the Lakota/Dakota flute tradition. Give it an original broad descending phrase with a high opening, long unhurried tones, and a repeated low landing. The tone is clear, rounded and breath-shaped, with restrained natural vibrato. Keep the existing dark sustained synth underneath and the deep drum very sparse. The flute adds a distinct human voice to the source's weight without making it pastoral.

cards.title: Straumr / Under the Current
cards.description: Keep the dark bowed-bass melody; a slow Hardanger-fiddle answer adds open-string drone and lingering sympathetic resonance.
cards.listen_for: Add a clearly audible Norwegian Hardanger fiddle in its lower and middle register, playing a slow, sustained answer to the source bass melody. Feature bowed double-stops against an open-string drone and the halo of sympathetic strings ringing after the bow moves on. Give the fiddle one exposed long answering phrase, then weave its resonance around the existing bowed bass. Use long bows with no dance rhythm or rapid ornaments.
